- Measurement: We measure uptime as percentage of successful request time within a UTC rolling 30-day window (we can include percentile-based reporting if you need it).
- Target: Our standard Hosted API for this tier is 99.95% monthly; we can discuss a narrow carve for scheduled maintenance windows versus unplanned events.
- Credits: We have a tiered credit table; I'll attach a first-pass redline for the Order Form SLA section (RI_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx).
- Response times: Our P1: 1 hour initial response / 4 hour remediation SLA target for enterprise customers (with on-call escalation to the SRE lead). P2/P3 follow standard business-hours SLAs; I'll outline exact windows in the doc.

Proposed 30-minute sync: Thu 9/20 10:30 PT. If that works, I'll include Karthik (contracts) and Lauren (customer success/ops) so we can close the exception matrix during the call.

Soojin — looping in legal/ops context. A few internal notes before we send the next version to Acme:

On measurement and uptime:
- We should avoid calendar-month definitions — stick with rolling 30-day as you suggested.
- For production cutovers, propose an exception lane: for the first 30 days post-cutover, we exclude scheduled maintenance from credit calculations if we provide 72 hours advance notice and schedule within an agreed blackout window.

On credits:
- Use discrete buckets (>=99.95%, 99.9-99.95%, <99.9%) with set credit percentages tied to monthly invoice. Avoid per-minute calculations that compound; Acme asked for examples, we can provide a worked example in the redline.

On response times & escalation matrix:
- P1: 1-hour acknowledgement, 4-hour mitigation target, with automatic internal escalation at T+2 hours to SRE lead (Marcus Lin) and at T+6 to Soojin/Head of Sales.
- P2: 4-hour acknowledge, 48-hour remediation window.

Action items for the sync:
- Lauren to confirm operational contact details and blackout dates from Acme (do we have their preferred maintenance windows?).
- Soojin to send RI_SLA_Redlines_v2.docx with the exception lane language and worked credit examples before the call.
